_meta.what: Calibration set for [memory] supersession_threshold and forget_relevance_floor (#260, #257).
why: Both values are cosine bars over the SAME embedding space, and both were wrong in opposite
directions: supersession at 0.85 admitted nothing (a paraphrase of the same fact scored
0.7917), while forget had no bar at all and deleted five unrelated facts on one call.
A bar chosen from a single anecdote is a guess wearing a measurement's clothes, so this set
exists to produce a distribution instead.
shape: Every text is written the way the MODEL stores facts (third person, whole sentences) rather
than the way a user says them, because that is the text the embedder actually sees. Taken
from real rows recovered from the M7 gate store, e.g. 'Ali drinks black coffee with no
sugar, and sometimes drinks a caramel latte with skim milk and sugar-free syrup.'

classes.contradictions: new REPLACES old. Must reach the §7.8 judge — this is the case supersession exists for.
classes.paraphrases: new RESTATES old. Near-duplicates; should also reach the judge (they are what 0.85 was aiming at).
classes.unrelated: new has nothing to do with old. Must NOT reach the judge, and must NOT be swept up by forget.

reading_it: The gate is a RECALL filter in front of a precision judge (§7.8): admitting an unrelated pair
costs one cheap TextModel call, while rejecting a contradiction costs a wrong memory forever.
The two error costs are not symmetric, and the chosen value should say so out loud.
If the classes overlap with no separating value, that IS the finding — report it, do not
split the difference and call it calibrated.
_meta.tier: 5 (SDS §14.7) — scored and tracked, never pass/fail. tools/eval_supersession.py always exits 0.
_meta.run_on: the Pi, with [adapters] embedder = local_minilm. FakeEmbedder is bag-of-words and has a different distribution; a value calibrated on it would be a number about the fake.
